recipes.name: Squash and Apple Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 pound butternut squash, peeled and chopped

steps.text: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add onion; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add squash, apples, potato, ginger, and white pepper; stir in water. Cover and bring to a boil; reduce heat to low and simmer until potatoes are tender, 12 to 15 minutes.

Transfer soup, in batches, to the bowl of a food processor or blender; pulse until smooth. Return puréed soup to the saucepan; repeat with remaining chunky soup. Stir apple cider and brown sugar into puréed soup; heat to boiling.
Garnish servings with a dollop of yogurt; sprinkle with pecans.

raw_recipe.headline: Squash and Apple Soup
raw_recipe.description: This squash and apple soup recipe, made with butternut squash, apples, potatoes, and ginger, is flavored with apple cider and yogurt for a hearty soup.

review.reviewBody: I made this recipe and was so impressed with it's texture and taste. A small bowl filled me up and satisfied me for hours. I used granny smith apples and couldn't believe the flavor of this soup! Great source of both fiber and vitamin c!

Definitely pre-cooked the squash, at least 5 min. in microwave, let it cool to peel sqash & also much easier to cut up. Sweet potato, boiled 1/4 apple slices drained for apple juice and sour cream for yogurt, no nuts so I added splash of Almond milk with each bowl with cinnamon sprinkled on top. Daughter said tastes like Pumkin Pie Soup, absolutely delicious!

I made this on a crisp fall evening for a light dinner.I omitted the potato cause I didn't have any, and used chicken broth instead of water, and added 1/2 t of salt and a T of seasoned rice vinegar.. I blended it in the pot with an immersion blender..no need for additional dirty dishes!Very tasty!

This was really good, I like the other reviewers added spice. I used my on pumpkin pie spice. I also added garlic and some pumpkin puree that I had in the refrigerator. I also added yogurt to the soup. I used 2 c apple cider and 2c water instead of 4c water to cook squash. Soup was excellent, the pumpkin pie spice smelled wonderful!!

I made this but added half a block of cream cheese to thicken Also I used frozen squash but needed to add an extra potato and a couple of carrots
THIS SOUP IS A KEEPER
This soup was great!!!! Only changes: Not water, used chicken broth. Added 1tsp Cinnamon. And roasted squash for 45min at 400deg.

This recipe calls for no seasoning other than ginger and white pepper, leaving this soup VERY bland if you don't at least add salt. This is why I only gave it 4 stars. I sauteed a clove of garlic with the onion, and added salt to taste. I stirred in a bit of butter before serving, as well, to give it a fuller flavor. My guests really enjoyed this soup.
I roasted the squash and apples first and used a ton more spices per everyone's suggestions. This is a total crowd pleaser!

Very tasty, although as usual for me I didn't follow the recipe exactly.....and I don't measure anything either. I was looking for a "sweet" version rather than a spicy or curried soup to match the recipe I've followed in the past, and just needed a reminder on the spices. I used chicken stock, added a dash of nutmeg, and omitted the potato. I also subbed half and half for the yogurt. Very good, it would have been perfect as written too.

I followed the advice of others to add some cinnamon and nutmeg. I also added 2 stalks of celery and 1 carrot, and substituted the water for chicken broth. I didn't bother adding yogurt at the end because I didn't have any. I LOVE this soup! It is so healthy, too!

I loved this recipe! In response to all those reviews about flavor, just add a teaspoon or so of cinnamon and maybe half or a quarter teaspoon of nutmeg. You'll be able to smell it when you have the right combo of spices, it will smell like apple pie.
I made as directed except I used ginger powder, about 3/4 of a TBS. The flavor was great, the texture very nice, and not too thick. Will repeat this again for sure.

I recently started a low sodium diet, and this was the first recipe I tried. I thought it was good, but as others have stated it's a little bland. Of course, I'm still adjusting to restricted sodium, so everything seems bland. Ha! The yogurt definitely helped. I'm thinking next time I will add more apples and maybe leave out the potato.

Super healthy, super hearty! The picture doesn't do it justice. I did not add apple cider and next time I would add an extra apple. I also used less ginger and sprinkled a 1/2 tsp to tsp of salt. 

When I served it, I sprinkled cinammon. It brings out the flavor of apples. If you are dieting, this is a great recipe to eat and feel full!!! :-)
I have been making this recipe for years. I do not find it bland at all and I make it as stated except for adding a little extra ginger. As others have noted it is very filling.

I used vegetable broth instead of water because of all the comments that it was bland. I enjoyed it, but I would prefer it more svavory than sweet. So, next time I will not add the brown sugar and maybe use some milk or cream in place of some of the liquid.
Delicious =) Very filling and the perfect addition to a cold winter night.

DELICIOUS!
At first I wasn't too thrilled... however, after a day of refridgeration, this has become my favorite soup!

This is just an outstanding recipe tho I did have to make some substitutions like with the butter for low fat and such and I did not have fresh ginger so I did use ground. Also I did not have apple cider and so I used pear juice which I did have and as for the yogurt I had vanilla low fat. And the squash I I had a buttercup squash but I tell you I put all that together and it came out the greatest soup. One thing is for sure you really must have the yogurt garnish or it will be bland. Oh, also I did not have white pepper I had a mixture of peppercorns and ground those fresh and used that instead. If you love squash you must try this soup.
Good but not great, my husband added lots of salt and pepper and I added a lot of garam masala.
